opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Operational funding
opportunities.amount: Part of per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 new / $5,000 established)
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered CU Boulder student org that is open to all students, and SOAC operational funding covers regular operating costs like those the club wants to fund. The Oct 14 priority deadline has passed, but late requests on BuffConnect are still accepted with no guaranteed hearing slot, and the last fall hearing is Nov 18. Meet your CSI liaison first and submit right away. If you miss the fall hearing, the next one is Jan 13. I couldn't confirm on the page that food or hardware are approved items or what the exact caps are.

Priority deadline passed; hearing slot not guaranteed

opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Event funding
opportunities.amount: Part of per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 new / $5,000 established)
opportunities.reasons: The club is a CU Boulder RSO that is open to all students, and SOAC funds events and operations, including food. The Oct 14 priority deadline has passed, but you can still submit on BuffConnect, though a hearing slot isn't guaranteed. The last fall hearing is Nov 18, and events need to be at least 30 days out. Meet your CSI liaison first. I couldn't confirm the per-year cap amounts on the page.

Priority deadline passed; hearing slot not guaranteed

opportunities.title: YC AI Student Starter Pack
opportunities.amount: Over $25,000 in credits per student (over $20,000 cloud plus over $5,000 GPT/Claude/Grok credits)
opportunities.reasons: Credits go to individual students who attend a YC university event (Fall 2025 onward), not to clubs, and there is no application or deadline. It's worth sharing with members if a YC event is held near CU Boulder, but the page doesn't say a club can host one, so don't count on it as club funding.
eligibility_flags: Credits go to individual students, not clubs
Requires attending a YC university event

opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Travel funding
opportunities.reasons: The club looks eligible as an open-to-all RSO, but this fund only covers travel (overnight, 60+ miles) for lodging, transport, airfare and registration fees, not food, AI tools or hardware. It's only worth pursuing if the club plans a conference or hackathon trip. The next deadline is Jan 4 for March travel, and the $5,000 cap wasn't confirmed on the page.
eligibility_flags: Must be open to all students

opportunities.title: OpenAI Student Collective
opportunities.reasons: The 2026 round closed August 10, 2026, so the club can't apply now. It is also a program for individual undergraduate Campus Leads working in pairs, not a club grant, and it requires 4–6 hours a week through June 2027. The perks (ChatGPT/Codex access, event funding) match the club's goals, so watch for a next round. I couldn't confirm that one will happen.
eligibility_flags: Individual undergraduate Campus Leads, not clubs
No cash for hardware or food stated

opportunities.title: Engineering Excellence Fund (EEF)
opportunities.provider: CU Boulder College of Engineering and Applied Science
opportunities.reasons: The fund is for engineering students, faculty and programs in the College of Engineering and Applied Science. Your club is open to all students, so it may not qualify unless it has an engineering tie. I couldn't confirm on the page whether non-engineering clubs can apply, the deadlines, or award sizes. Research hardware might fit, but food and AI tool giveaways probably don't.

opportunities.title: HackCU
opportunities.reasons: The page shows the HackCU World Cup Hackathon on March 7-8, 2026, which has already passed. It is a free event for individual students, and the listed prizes are non-cash (AI subscriptions and merch). It is not funding for the club's food, tools or hardware. Check later for next year's event if members want to compete.
eligibility_flags: Event for individual students, not club funding

opportunities.title: Boulder Startup Week 2026
opportunities.reasons: The page describes Boulder Startup Week 2026 as a free conference held May 4-8, 2026, which has already happened. It lists no funding, sponsorship program or application for student clubs. You could still contact the organizers about future events, but this isn't a funding opportunity.

opportunities.title: CU Boulder and Techstars partnership
opportunities.reasons: This is a news announcement about a CU Boulder–Techstars partnership, not a funding program. It mentions no grants, sponsorships or club funding, and no application or deadline for clubs. The only application it links to is for startup founders (Techstars Boulder Accelerator), which doesn't match the club's needs for food, AI tools and hardware.

opportunities.title: NSF FINDERS Foundry
opportunities.reasons: Only nonprofits, state/local governments, universities (applying for faculty) and tribal nations can submit, so a student club can't apply directly. The program funds K-12 AI education projects, not club food, AI tools or hardware.
eligibility_flags: Team needs K-12 educators, technologists and researchers

opportunities.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments
opportunities.reasons: The principal investigator must be an engineering department chair or a senior university leader, so a student club can't lead this grant. It funds department-wide engineering education reform, not food, AI tools or hardware for a club.

# AI Club: SOAC Operational Funding Request

## Organization
AI Club is a registered student organization at CU Boulder, founded about 2 years ago and open to all students. We have 100 members and 800+ people on our email list.

## Mission and Purpose
We bring in speakers to teach CU students and faculty about evolving technology, especially AI. Our regular meetings draw about 100 attendees, and we also host speaker events. Our speaker engagements have included G2 and Techstars.

## Request
Amount requested: [[MISSING: total dollar amount, within the SOAC per-year cap for our status (new vs. established)]]

| Item | Purpose | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Food at meetings | Regular member meetings (about 100 attendees) | [[MISSING: cost per meeting and number of meetings]] |
| AI tools for students | [[ASSUMED: software subscriptions or licenses held by the club and made available to any student]] | [[MISSING: tools, vendor, quantity, cost]] |
| Hardware for research time | [[ASSUMED: equipment stored on campus and used for club research and projects]] | [[MISSING: hardware list, cost, storage location]] |

## How This Supports Our Mission
Operations funding covers regular expenses that let us carry out our mission. Food keeps meetings accessible. AI tools and hardware give students hands-on access to the technology our speakers discuss. [[MISSING: how many students are expected to use the tools and hardware, and how access will be shared]]

## Open Membership
AI Club is open to all CU Boulder students. [[MISSING: confirmation that there are no membership selection criteria]]

## Timeline
We are submitting after the Oct. 14 priority deadline and ask to be heard at the Nov. 18 hearing if a slot is available. [[MISSING: BuffConnect submission date and CSI liaison meeting confirmation]]

## Requirements checklist
- [ ] Must be a registered student organization open to all CU Boulder students
- [ ] Submit the request through BuffConnect
- [ ] Operations funding covers regular operating expenses for the org's mission; items should be for organizational (not personal) use and stored on campus where possible
- [ ] Oct 14 priority deadline has passed; late submissions are accepted but a hearing slot is not guaranteed
- [ ] Last fall 2026 SOAC hearing is Wed. Nov. 18; no funding hearings after that date until the first spring hearing on Wed. Jan. 13, 2027
- [ ] Deadlines are subject to change; confirm on the SOAC page
- [ ] Meet your CSI liaison before submitting
assumptions: AI tools are software subscriptions/licenses held by the club and shared with any student
Hardware is equipment stored on campus for club research and projects

## Mission and Impact
AI Club brings in speakers to teach CU students and faculty about evolving technology, especially AI. The club has secured engagements with G2 and Techstars.

## Event Description
[[MISSING: event name, date (must be at least 30 days out), location, and speaker]].
